sections.title: Slots, .use() and gates
sections.explain: A slot is a named hole in a chain: .use("fx") marks it, hooks.bind fills it with a hook. A gate says when the binding is open: "@17b" from bar 17 on, "<17b" before bar 17, "9b..17b" bars 9 to 16. Outside its gate the slot bypasses. hooks.def names a reusable chain.

examples.title: A slot and a hook
examples.code:
hooks.def("murk", { chain: [["lpf", 400], ["room", 0.4]] })
hooks.bind("fx", "murk")
$: note("c2 eb2 g2 bb2").s("sawtooth").use("fx")

examples.title: Drop-in at bar 3 (@3b)
examples.code:
hooks.bind("fx", [["distort", 2], ["hpf", 120]], "@3b")
$: s("sawtooth").note("c2*4").use("fx")

examples.title: Before bar 3 (<3b)
examples.code:
hooks.def("murk", { chain: [["lpf", 300]] })
hooks.bind("fx", "murk", "<3b")
$: note("c3 e3 g3 b3").s("triangle").use("fx")

examples.title: Range with fallback (2b..4b)
examples.code:
hooks.def("murk", { chain: [["lpf", 400]] })
hooks.def("open", { chain: [["lpf", 4000]] })
hooks.bind("fx", "open", "2b..4b", { else: "murk" })
$: note("c2 eb2 g2 bb2").s("sawtooth").use("fx")

sections.title: .tap(), .wire(), variables and decorators
sections.explain: .tap("name") publishes a pattern so others can read it with tap("name") or facets like tap("kick:env"). .wire(param, tap, opts) drives a param from a tap. hooks.let defines a variable (gated assignments act like a key change). Decorators wrap hooks: every(4)[h], mix(0.3)[h], h | g.

examples.title: Tap to param: ducking
examples.code:
$: s("sine").note("c1*4").decay(0.2).tap("kick")
$: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").wire("gain", "kick:env", { range: [1, 0.3], op: "mul", r: 0.25 })

examples.title: Variable with a key change
examples.code:
hooks.let("root", 48)
hooks.let("root", 51, "@3b")
$: note(tap("root").add("0 3 7 10")).s("sawtooth")
$: note(tap("root").sub(12)).s("triangle").struct("x*2")

examples.title: Decorated binding
examples.code:
hooks.def("murk", { chain: [["lpf", 500]] })
hooks.bind("fx", "every(2)[murk]")
$: note("c3 eb3 g3").s("sawtooth").use("fx")

sections.title: Lanes: tags, selections and lane-scoped taps
sections.explain: A lane is one labelled pattern (drums: ... or $: ...); its label is its id. .tags("drums", "wet") puts tags on every event of a lane (same as chained .tag("drums").tag("wet")). tagged(selector) selects events by tag, #lane id, & (and), | (or), ! (not), ( ) and *, and its ops act on them across all lanes without touching the lane code: .fx(x => ...), .gain(g), .orbit(n), .mute(gate), .solo(gate). Two solo() selections play the union. .tap("x") inside a lane publishes lane/x: two lanes may both publish x; a read tap("x") finds its own lane first, tap("drums/x") names another lane. Reading a tap of another lane needs { export: true } on the publisher; without it open mode (default) still works and the check reports W_LANE_IMPLICIT_EXPORT, while lanes.closed() makes it E_LANE_PRIVATE. A tap keeps a query cache (32 spans, cleared on every edit, control change and registry change), so many readers share one computation of everything upstream of the tap. Also checked: E_LANE_DUP (one label twice) and W_LANE_ORBIT_FX (two lanes on one orbit with different room size or delay settings). Built for the editor and the graph (L4): the model records a lane's tags, its split branches, its sends and returns (named buses, never bus numbers), every tagged(...) statement as a selection and every capture(...) declaration; the graph shows lane cards with their tags, one bus node per named bus, one selection chip per tagged(...) statement listing its matching lanes, and refuses a wire out of a split branch (E_LANE_CROSS) with the fixes Export tap and Add send. Completion: inside a branch callback only bus-safe controls (room, lpf, gain, struct ...) are offered, never s, n, note; tagged(" offers tags and #lane ids; .send(" and ret(" offer bus names; recall("name: offers only the facets that capture records. Atom types tag, selector, busname and capture compile to single-quoted strings, so tagged(atoms.wetDrums) works. Pads can toggle a selection's mute or solo and keep working when its statement moves. AUDIO (built, #75): .split(f, g, ...) renders everything before it once and gives each branch f a bus reader of that one render, so effects run in parallel without re-triggering voices (.layer costs one voice per note per branch; a split costs the source voices plus one reader voice per branch and per cycle). A branch is written x => x.effect(...): it may add effects, gain, pan, orbit and structure (x.struct("x*16") is a rhythmic gate on the lane audio); it may not set s, n, note, freq, bus or dry (E_LANE_SOURCE). Effects in a branch act on the lane sum (one filter or distortion for all notes), not per note: put per-note effects before the split. Options as the last argument: { mix: [1, 0.5, 0.25] } (branch postgains) and { pre: true } (keep the source's direct path too). .merge(m => ...) sums the branches on a second bus and applies m and everything written after it to that one reader; an effect written after .split(...) without .merge is added to each branch separately (W_LANE_POST_SPLIT for non-linear ones such as shape, crush, compressor). Splits nest (a branch may split). .send("name", amount) sends the lane to a named bus (0..1, default 1) and ret("name") starts a lane that plays that bus (several lanes may send, several may return); a send with no return is W_BUS_NO_RETURN, a loop is E_LANE_CYCLE, ret inside a branch or a tap of a branch read elsewhere is E_LANE_CROSS. tagged(sel).send(name, amount) sends every lane whose literal .tags(...) or #id match. .wire("lpf", "bus:name", { depthabs: 600 }) modulates a control with the raw audio of a named bus (bmod): cutoff = base + (signal + dc) x depthabs / 0.3 (bipolar; depth is a multiple of the current value, depthabs is absolute; a slow LFO is a sine with .freq(0.25), note("c1") is an audio-rate 32.7 Hz tone). Bus numbers are allocated by the compiler (lane buses from 64 in source order, named buses from 512 in name order) and are never written by hand: user .bus(n) from 64 up is E_BUS_RANGE. It all compiles to plain Strudel on superdough's own bus, busgain, dry and s("bus") (10 ms cross-fade between cycles, measured seamless); a host without the bus sound raises E_LANE_HOST and is never silently replaced by .layer. IN THE GRAPH (Graph view, #78): every lane is a card with its tags as chips; a chip's Mute or Solo writes (or removes) one tagged("tag").mute() / .solo() statement, so it plays from the next cycle; a split is drawn inside the card as a fan (one audio bar in, one row per branch, the sum or merge out) with + Branch, fold, and Voices (source + reader voices per cycle from the engine, against what .layer would build); a bus is one node with its sends (amounts edited in place) and returns; an exported tap is a port on the card edge, a tap inside a branch only inside the fan, and wiring it to another lane is refused with E_LANE_CROSS and the fixes Export tap and Add send. The Outline pane lists lanes (filter by tag), tags with Mute / Solo, split fans, buses and captures, so every action works from the keyboard. CAPTURE (built, #76): capture(name, picker, { window: "1b..3b" | last: "2b", what, live, max }) records what the picked lanes (a selector), an event tap ("lane/tap", events only) or master play; nothing is added to the program. recall("name") is the captured haps as a pattern looping with the capture's length (opts { at, once, gate }), recall("name:level") a 0..1 signal from the audio level (RMS per 1/64 cycle), recall("name:onset" | ":gate" | ":<control>") the event facets, recall("name:audio") and pat.from("name") the captured audio as the sample cap_<name> (pat.s("cap_name"); Strudel's slice needs its index pattern: .slice(8, "0 3 2 1 4 7 6 5")). A window capture is empty until it closes; a pure capture (no ctl(), pad tap or input in the picked lanes) is resolved ahead by an offline pass and is usable from cycle 0, a live one from until + 1 cycle (E_CAPTURE_EARLY when a gate opens sooner); a rolling capture shows the last length before the previous cycle boundary and strudelCraft.lanesCapture.freeze(name, at) / thaw(name, at) hold it (journaled). Audio and level need the site (offline render of the picked lanes through strudelCraft.lanesCapture.host.resolve). Errors: E_CAPTURE_LAYER LIVE EARLY CYCLE LIMIT MEMORY NAME and W_CAPTURE_TEMPO. Not built yet and marked coming: audio of bus:<name> and of rolling captures, the CLI commands strudel capture / lanes / render / stems / events for lane programs, and sending a tag to a pad from the graph. Built: Remake and every offline render run the capture passes first (beforeRender hook); the Graph view's capture node has Bounce to takes (an audio take with meta.from in the Record list), Freeze / Thaw for rolling captures (journaled, at a cycle) and Use as sample (registers cap_<name>, shows it with Copy, inserts one lane s("x").from("<name>").loopAt(<cycles>) as one undo step); on bus: and rolling captures Bounce and Use as sample stay disabled as coming. docs/LANES.md.

examples.title: Tags, then one selection for a group
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4, hh*8").tags("drums")
snare: s("~ sd").tags("drums", "wet")
keys: note("c e g").s("piano").tags("keys", "wet")
tagged("drums & !wet").fx(x => x.hpf(40))

examples.title: Select by lane id or tag
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4").tags("drums")
keys: note("c3 e3 g3").s("triangle").tags("keys")
pad: note("c4").s("sawtooth").tags("wet")
tagged("#keys | wet").fx(x => x.lpf(900))

examples.title: Mute a group for bars 3 and 4
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4, hh*8").tags("drums")
bass: note("c2*4").s("sawtooth").tags("bass")
tagged("drums").mute("3b..5b")

examples.title: Lane-scoped taps, exported across lanes
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4").bank("RolandTR909").tap("hits", { export: true })
bass: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").gain(tap("drums/hits:env", { r: 0.2 }).range(1, 0.4))

examples.title: Closed mode: only exported taps cross lanes
examples.code:
lanes.closed()
drums: s("bd*4").tap("kick", { export: true })
bass: note("c2*4").s("sawtooth").gain(tap("kick:env").range(1, 0.4))

examples.title: Parallel effects on one render (.split)
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4, hh*8").lpf(4000)
  .split(dry => dry,
         wet => wet.room(0.9).rsize(6).lpf(900),
         grit => grit.crush(5).hpf(2000).gain(0.4))

examples.title: Merge: one effect on the sum of the branches
examples.code: drums: s("bd*4, hh*8").split(d => d, w => w.room(0.8)).merge(m => m.shape(0.3)).gain(0.9)

examples.title: Rhythmic gate on a pad, source rendered once
examples.code:
pad: note("<c3 eb3 g3 bb3>").s("supersaw").release(1)
  .split(g => g.struct("x*16").decay(0.04).sustain(0), d => d.gain(0.3))

examples.title: Sends and a shared return (.send, ret)
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4").send("verb", 0.3)
keys: note("c e g").s("piano").send("verb", 0.6)
verb: ret("verb").room(1).rsize(8).lpf(3000)

examples.title: Group send by tag
examples.code:
drums: s("bd*4, hh*8").tags("drums")
keys: note("c e g").s("piano").tags("harm", "wet")
verb: ret("verb").room(1).rsize(8)
tagged("drums | wet").send("verb", 0.5)

examples.title: A bus as a slow LFO (.wire to bus:name)
examples.code:
lfo: s("sine").freq(0.25).slow(4).dry(0).send("mod", 2)
lead: note("c3").s("sawtooth").slow(4).lpf(800).wire("lpf", "bus:mod", { depthabs: 600 })
examples.explain: Order of operations: (1) the lfo lane is an ordinary source, a 0.25 Hz sine (.freq(0.25), one sweep every 4 s); .dry(0) mutes its direct output, so it is silent. (2) The compiler gives the lane a lane bus and the source plays into it. (3) The .send reader forwards that bus to the named bus "mod" at the send amount (2, the sine is quiet: a unit send moves the cutoff only about 0.48 x depthabs). (4) .wire("lpf", "bus:mod", opts) is bmod: it reads the named bus on the lead, so each lead voice adds (signal + dc) x depthabs / 0.3 Hz to its cutoff. The signal is bipolar (a sine swings both ways around the 800 Hz base, here about 200 to 1400 Hz). depth is a multiple of the current cutoff (depth: 1 means 800), depthabs is in Hz; a negative depth inverts; dc shifts the centre (dc: 0.15 adds depthabs / 2). A pitch like note("c1") is 32.7 Hz, an audio-rate tone, not an LFO: use .freq(hz) for a slow one. Measured (superdough 1.3.0, offline render): the lead's spectral centroid sweeps 235 to 750 Hz (static cutoffs 200 and 1400 give 212 and 764) at 0.26 Hz. In offline renders the lead voice starts modulating about one cycle in.
flow: s("sine").freq(0.25): the source voice; dry(0) keeps it off the speakers
the source plays into its own lane bus
reads bus 64 and forwards it x2 (send amount) to the named bus
named bus carrying the raw sine, bipolar

examples.title: A bus as an audio-rate modulator: growl (.wire, depthabs)
examples.code:
growl: note("c1").s("sine").slow(4).dry(0).send("growl", 1)
lead: note("c2").s("sawtooth").slow(4).lpf(600).wire("lpf", "bus:growl", { depthabs: 1200 })
examples.explain: The same route as the slow LFO, but the source is note("c1") = 32.7 Hz, so the cutoff is modulated about 33 times a second: that is not a sweep you hear as movement but a growl (sidebands and a buzzing timbre). Measured (offline render, held c2 saw): the lead's short-time centroid modulates at 32.7 Hz and ranges 43 to 635 Hz (65 Hz fundamental, std 188 against 111 unmodulated); half-harmonic sideband energy is 0.87 of the harmonic energy against 0.00 without the wire. Keep depthabs modest: the original relative form { depth: 600 } meant 600 x the cutoff (480000 Hz of swing, peak 31.8 in the render); the signal is also bipolar, so the cutoff is driven to its floor on every negative half-wave.
flow: forwards bus 64 to named bus growl at send 1

examples.title: Capture a bar group and reuse it as a sample (capture, .from)

Rolling capture of the last two bars (recall)

sections.title: Inline controls and mapping
sections.explain: ctl("name", {type, min, max}) declares a control and returns its value as a pattern. It shows up under the editor as soon as the code compiles (no Play needed) and on the Perform board; slider(v, min, max) works too. hooks.map('ctl', 'param', { range, curve, op, priority }) sends one control to params it never touches in the code: the map is applied to the events of that param as they are queried, so one knob can move several layers. The control has to exist when the map line runs (declare it with ctl() first, or map it in Perform with Learn), and the line only counts while it is still in an editor. Automation lanes recorded in Perform play back through the same values. Each control gets a generated id from where it sits in the code (e.g. k3f9a2c at L0/note.s.lpf#0), so it keeps its value while you edit. Long-press (or hover/focus) a control to see its id, path, value, range and mappings; its source is highlighted in the editor, and putting the caret on the call makes the control glow. Tap a number, name or chord in the code to edit it in place (drag numbers to scrub); changes apply at once. Ranges are never assumed to be 0..1: tap a control's number to type an exact value (1.5k, -6 dB, 2:30), "Extend range to fit" widens it, and "Range…" in its sheet sets min, max, step, curve and clamp. hooks.map sends one control to several destinations.

examples.title: A cutoff knob
examples.code: $: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").lpf(ctl("cutoff", { type: "knob", min: 200, max: 4000 }))

examples.title: Strudel slider()
examples.code: $: note("c3 e3 g3").s("triangle").gain(slider(0.6, 0, 1))

examples.title: Inspect a control (long-press the knob)
examples.code: $: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").lpf(slider(800, 20, 20000)).room(ctl("space", { type: "knob", min: 0, max: 1 }))

examples.title: Type past the range (tap the number, enter 5000)
examples.code: $: note("c3 e3").s("sawtooth").lpf(slider(0.5, 0, 1).mul(4000))

examples.title: Map one knob onto another layer
examples.code:
$: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").gain(ctl("macro", { type: "knob", min: 0, max: 1, default: 0.6 }))
$: s("hh*8").room(0.1)
hooks.map('macro', 'room', { range: [0, 0.8] })

sections.title: Inline visuals (_pianoroll, _scope ...)
sections.explain: An underscore visual draws inside the code, in a band directly below the line that calls it, as on strudel.cc: _pianoroll, _punchcard, _spiral, _scope, _tscope, _fscope, _wordfall, _pitchwheel. The band is as wide as the editor, scrolls with the code and pushes the lines below it down; its height is reserved as soon as the code compiles, so Play does not move anything. Pass { height: 200 } for a taller band (60 to 600 px). Without the underscore (.pianoroll(), .scope()) the visual draws behind the whole page instead. .color() tints events in the visuals and in the code highlighting.

examples.title: Piano roll under its line
examples.code:
$: note("c3 e3 g3 b3").s("triangle").color("cyan magenta")
  ._pianoroll()

examples.title: Two bands: piano roll and scope
examples.code:
$: note("<c3 eb3> g3 bb3").s("sawtooth").lpf(900)
  ._pianoroll({ height: 160 })
$: s("sine").note("c2*2").decay(0.3)
  ._scope()

examples.title: Punchcard and spiral
examples.code:
$: note("c3 [e3 g3] a3 g3").s("triangle")._punchcard()
$: note("c4 e4 g4").s("sine").gain(0.4)._spiral()

sections.title: Pads and the control board
sections.explain: Perform (key 5) holds pad banks and control boards as tabs. In Perform mode a pad press is quantised (bar by default) and journaled; Edit mode opens the pad sheet to set its target, mode, quantise and choke, and lays the board out (sizes, move, place, remove). Boards show every control with its mapping; tap Map... to remap, or Learn and move a control to write one hooks.map(...) line into the playing editor (Unlearn removes it). "Rec lane" records the next control you move for 1/2/4 bars as an automation lane; the looper strip records, overdubs and replays pad takes; "Tabs ..." adds, renames and reorders tabs and switches scenes (rows/columns); "Save to library" stores a bank, board, take or lane as a component.

sections.title: Library components
sections.explain: A component (fragment, track, set, song) is a saved model with exports, versioned by revision: every save is a new rev, so a reference like "pad@1" is pinned content. Components come from Graph (key 7: drag nodes; two fingers to move the view; select nodes, Save to library / Collapse to subgraph) or from Perform ("Save to library" for a bank, board, take or lane); they live in this browser. hooks.inst("pad@1", { as: "pad2", args: {...}, gate, remap }) drops one revision into the program under its own namespace, and hooks.bind(slot, 'lib:warmth@1(0.4)') binds a saved fragment's hook into a slot. The two examples below load into Rack without playing because they only run once their component is in your library (an unknown reference reports E_COMPONENT_MISSING).

examples.title: Instance a saved component (needs pad@1 in this browser's library)
examples.code:
$: hooks.inst("pad@1", { as: "pad2" })
$: s("bd*4")

examples.title: Bind a saved fragment into a slot (needs warmth@1)
examples.code:
hooks.bind('fx', 'lib:warmth@1(0.4)')
$: note("c2 eb2 g2").s("sawtooth").use("fx")

sections.title: word() vocals
sections.explain: word("<call me baby>") plays your vocal word bank (vox_<word> samples) with mini-notation; "baby:2" picks the third take. syl("0 1 2") plays syllables in lyric order. vowel() is a formant filter (it does not shift formants). A demo bank (espeak-ng speech) loads on first use; voxBank('call-me-baby') switches to the owner's vocal bank (keys it lacks fall back to demo), voxBank(url) loads a strudel.json, voxBank() picks a local folder, voxBank.list() shows banks with kind, counts, pitches and licence, voxBank.words(name) lists a bank's entries. voxBank('ljspeech') is ~500 common English and lyric words from LJSpeech (public domain, 1-3 takes each, loaded lazily per word); voxBank('vocalset') is sustained sung vowels from VocalSet (CC BY 4.0), keys vs_<vowel>_<technique>, pitched for note(). voxBank('sung') is 200 English words sung at five pitches two octaves wide (d#3 a3 d#4 a4 d#5), rendered offline with SoulX-Singer (Apache-2.0) and a VocalSet timbre prompt (CC BY 4.0): note() plays the nearest sung pitch and retunes at most 3 semitones, so it stays a sung voice over d#3 to d#5; keys it lacks fall back to demo. Word names complete inside the quotes from the ACTIVE bank (the detail names the bank, takes and pitches; keys it lacks fall back to demo), and s("vs_ completes the vocalset keys; the Banks section below shows what each bank holds. .note() on a bank retunes by speed, so formants move with the pitch; formant-preserving takes are pre-rendered at build time by the wordbank CLI (--formant-steps, pyworld) and missing lyric words can be filled by opt-in TTS (--tts-fallback); neither is in the site banks yet. word(...).note(x).formant(true) picks the pre-rendered variant vox_<word>_f<semi> nearest to the shift (note minus the word's sung base note), then fine-tunes the residual (at most 50 cents) with speed; on a bank without variants (every site bank today) it plays the plain note() retune and shows one warning toast.

examples.title: Words in a pattern
examples.code: $: word("<call me baby>").vowel("<a o>")

examples.title: Call Me Baby bank, retuned
examples.code:
await voxBank('call-me-baby')
$: word("<call me baby>").note("<c3 e3 g3>")

examples.title: LJSpeech bank (public domain)
examples.code:
await voxBank('ljspeech')
$: word("<love fire night>").note("<c3 e3 g3>")

examples.title: VocalSet vowels as a pad (CC BY 4.0)
examples.code:
await voxBank('vocalset')
$: s("<vs_a vs_o vs_e_trill>").note("<c3 g3 e4>").slow(2).room(.6)

examples.title: Sung words (SoulX-Singer render)
examples.code:
await voxBank('sung')
$: word("<love fire night tonight>").note("<a3 c4 e4 a4>").room(.4)

examples.title: Formant-preserving retune (variants need a --formant-steps bank; else plain retune + one warning)
examples.code: $: word("<call me baby>").note("<c3 e3 g3>").formant(true)

sections.title: Banks: what you can type
sections.explain: The Banks button (top of this view), Ctrl+K > Banks or the Banks workspace pane lists every vox bank: demo, call-me-baby, ljspeech, vocalset, sung, banks you loaded with voxBank(url) or a folder, and vox-bank packs. Each shows its kind (word bank: word("baby:1"); sound bank: s("vs_a")), word and clip counts, pitches, licence and attribution, and which one is active. Open a bank to search and filter its entries (words with their takes, pitches and durations; vocalset keys vs_<vowel>_<technique>): tap a pitch or take to hear that clip without any code, tap the snippet to insert it into the Rack code (with the voxBank line it needs), tap Use to switch the active bank; the panel shows the matching voxBank('name') line. Bank files are read through the pack loader only when opened, and audio only when you audition. Completions inside word(" follow the active bank; hovering or long-pressing word or voxBank shows the active bank and its size.

examples.title: Switch bank, then type what it lists
examples.code:
await voxBank('sung')
$: word("<baby love night>").note("<a3 d#4 a4>")

examples.title: A take at its own pitch (as the panel inserts it)
examples.code:
await voxBank('call-me-baby')
$: word("baby:1").note("a#4")

examples.title: Sound bank keys
examples.code:
await voxBank('vocalset')
$: s("<vs_a vs_o_forte>").note("c3").slow(2)

examples.title: List banks and entries in code
examples.code:
const sung = await voxBank.words('sung') // [{name, key, takes, notes, dur}]
console.log(voxBank.list().map((b) => b.name + ' ' + b.words + ' words'))
$: word(sung.slice(0, 4).map((e) => e.name).join(' '))

sections.title: Ghost text and Tab
sections.explain: Type in the editor: a dimmed continuation appears at the cursor. Tab (or the Tab chip on phones) accepts it, Esc dismisses it, Ctrl/Alt+] cycles alternatives. Tab also accepts the selected popup item, and indents when nothing is suggested. Accepting replaces the word or value under the cursor instead of adding to it: existing brackets, arguments and later chain calls are kept, an accept that is already there just moves the cursor, and one Ctrl+Z undoes it. Until you accept, a suggestion changes nothing (no edit, no history, no re-run); it disappears when you tap elsewhere, scroll, switch view, press Esc or wait 5 seconds, and comes back when you type or press Ctrl+Space.

examples.title: Try: type .lpf( then Tab
examples.code: $: note("c2 eb2").s("sawtooth")

sections.title: Transport range, workspace and palette
sections.explain: The stage has a position slider: 'c 12.3/64.0·00:24/02:08' (fixed decimals and widths, so nothing jitters) is current cycle / end cycle · elapsed / end time (end = loop End, or the play-time clamp). Start, End and Go-to take a cycle or m:ss; the unit button cycles cycle / bar / m:ss, converted with the live cps. Play time is clamped (20 min default, timer button) with a fade and a +5 min override. W toggles the workspace; Ctrl+K (or the floating button on phones) opens the command palette, which also loads layouts. Code can add palette actions and seek. Install app (palette > App, the ? dialog or the overflow menu) installs Strudel Craft as an app: on Android Chrome it opens the install prompt, elsewhere an Add to Home Screen hint; installed, it starts full screen, works offline after the first visit (the editor and Play too; a sample bank not cached yet shows an Offline toast) and has Rack / Stack / Record / Perform shortcuts on a long-press of its icon.

examples.title: Add a palette action
examples.code:
strudelCraft.palette.register({ id: 'my.drop', group: 'Mine', title: 'Jump to the drop', run: () => strudelCraft.range.seek(16) })
$: s("bd*4, hh*8").bank("RolandTR909")

examples.title: Loop cycles 4 to 8
examples.code:
Object.assign(strudelCraft.range.state, { start: 4, end: 8, loop: true })
$: note("<c3 eb3 g3 bb3>*2").s("sawtooth").lpf(800)

examples.title: Load a layout

strudelCraft.workspace.load('Perform')
$: s("bd ~ sd ~")

examples.title: Install as an app
examples.code:
strudelCraft.pwa.install()
$: s("bd*4, hh*8").bank("RolandTR909")

sections.title: Copy code and share links
sections.explain: Every code field (the Rack editor, the Stack program and each example block here) has a copy button at its top-right corner. One tap copies the whole program from the editor's document (not what is drawn on screen), so a folded, highlighted or erroring program copies exactly as written; the button shows a check mark and a Copied toast. Hold the button (or right-click it, or press Down on it) for more: Copy selection (only when text is selected), Copy as a shareable link (a URL with the code compressed into its #code/ hash; opening it loads the code into Rack without running it until you press Play; links hold up to 256 kB of code, and an oversized or damaged link loads nothing and says why in a toast) and Copy with controls and state (a recipe JSON with the code, control values, bindings, Perform model and settings, the same format the Record panel writes, with includes.code only). Ctrl+K > Copy runs the same actions on the visible editor. Where the browser blocks the clipboard API a hidden text field copy is used instead. Keyboard: Tab to the button, Enter or Space copies, Down or Up opens the menu, Esc closes it; these keys never start playback while the button or its menu has focus.

sections.title: Record panel and recipes
sections.explain: The record button in the transport (or Ctrl+K > Record, or the Record workspace pane) opens one Record panel. Tick Audio, Events (lanes, pads, control moves) and Code-state, then one Record captures them together; Cycles starts and stops on cycle boundaries so the take loops. Every take is a recipe: versioned JSON (schemas/recipe.v1.json) holding the program, controls, settings, seed, timing, event stream and pinned dependencies (Strudel bundle hash, packs with commit + content hashes, sample and vox banks by hash), with the audio as optional outputs. Remake regenerates the audio from the recipe after you approve its dependencies and checks the result against the stored audio hash (bit for bit, or by a level fingerprint for noise and other takes that are not bit-exact, which it says); a tampered or unpinned ref refuses the load. Imported recipes stay inert until Remake. Downloads: the recipe JSON, WAV 16/24, and a WebM/opus copy of realtime audio takes (where the browser's MediaRecorder supports opus; its length is within about 0.1 s of the cycle cut). The capture tap has no outputs and adds nothing to what you hear.

examples.title: Arm a 4-cycle take with audio, events and code-state
examples.code:
strudelCraft.capture.configure({ mode: 'cycles', n: 4, audio: true, events: true, code: true, name: 'arp-loop' })
strudelCraft.capture.open()
$: note("<c3 eb3 g3 bb3>*4").s("sawtooth").lpf(900).room(.3)

examples.code:
strudelCraft.capture.configure({ audio: false, events: true, code: true, name: 'moves' })
strudelCraft.capture.open()
$: note("c3 e3 g3 b3").s("sawtooth").cutoff(ctl("cut", { type: "knob", min: 200, max: 4000, unit: "Hz" }))

examples.code:
strudelCraft.capture.configure({ n: 8, fold: true, bits: 24, name: 'pad-8c' })
strudelCraft.capture.open()
// then tap Render exact 8 cycles; Remake re-checks its hash later
$: note("<c3 eb3>/2").s("triangle").attack(.4).release(1.5)

const off = strudelCraft.capture.beforeRender(async (recipe, { code }) => { /* render cap_<name> audio before the offline pass */ })
await strudelCraft.capture.addTake({ name: 'groove', L, R, sr: 48000, cps: 0.5, cycles: 2, from: 'groove' })

sections.title: Atoms: named, typed strings
sections.explain: An atom gives a magic string one typed, parameterised definition: atom("kick4", { type: "mini", params: { n: { shape: "number", min: 1, max: 16, default: 4 } }, body: "bd*${n}" }) and then atoms.kick4 or atoms.kick4({ n: 8 }) anywhere a string would go. References compile away before Strudel sees the program: pattern types (mini, sound, note, chord, scale) become double-quoted strings, name types (gate, point, tapref, slot, hook, name) single-quoted. Ops compose without hand-written brackets: .stack() .seq() .alt() .rep() .slow() .euclid() on patterns, .union() .shift() on gates, .after() .before() .to() on points, .facet() .in() on refs. The compile pass, types, schema and ids are built (site/engine/atoms.js, docs/ATOMS.md, #61); extract / parse / inline and the catalog namespaces atoms.snd.bd, atoms.bank.RolandTR909, atoms.scale.minor({ root: "C" }), atoms.chord.m7({ root: "C" }) (no declaration needed) are built too (site/engine/atoms-migrate.js, #62); Open in strudel.cc and Copy inline the program because atoms exist only in this toolkit. The consumers are built too (#63): references compile away before every evaluation (so these examples play), completion offers only the atoms whose type fits the argument position, atoms. lists names and the catalog namespaces, atoms.kick4( shows signature help with the param range, a string literal an atom already produces offers "use atoms.name", and an argument of a reference is a normal literal site (scrub, chips, steps) clamped to the atom's own range. Pads, board cells and maps may address their target by { "$atom": id }, so a rename costs one edit. Tap a reference (or Enter with the caret on it) for its popover: compiled string, param editors, Edit definition, Derive, Detach, Go to card. In the Graph view each referenced atom is one card with its reference count, type badge, preview and editors (a derived reference such as atoms.kick4({ n: 8 }) gets its own card linked to kick4); unreferenced atoms are never drawn, and the Atoms button lists them on demand for the armed port, 50 per page (#64).

examples.title: Declare and reference
examples.code:
atom("kick4", { type: "mini", params: { n: { shape: "number", min: 1, max: 16, step: 1, default: 4 } }, body: "bd*${n}" })
atom("kick", { type: "name", body: "kick" })
$: s(atoms.kick4).tap(atoms.kick)
$: s(atoms.kick4({ n: 8 })).gain(0.6)

examples.title: Compose instead of retyping
examples.code:
atom("kick4", { type: "mini", body: "bd*4" })
atom("backbeat", { type: "mini", body: "~ sd ~ sd" })
$: s(atoms.kick4.stack(atoms.backbeat).slow(2))

examples.title: One name for a gate and a tap ref
examples.code:
atom("drop", { type: "point", body: "17b" })
atom("kickEnv", { type: "tapref", body: "kick:env" })
hooks.bind("fx", "murk", atoms.drop.after())
$: note("c2*8").s("sawtooth").wire("gain", atoms.kickEnv, { range: [1, 0.3], op: "mul" })

examples.title: Catalog atoms need no declaration
examples.code:
$: s(atoms.snd.bd).bank(atoms.bank.RolandTR909)
$: n("0 2 4").scale(atoms.scale.minor({ root: "C" }))
$: chord(atoms.chord.m7({ root: "D" })).voicing()

examples.title: Popover, cards and the browser
examples.code:
atom("kick4", { type: "mini", params: { n: { shape: "number", min: 1, max: 16, step: 1, default: 4 } }, body: "bd*${n}" })
atom("loud", { type: "mini", body: "0.8 0.6" })
// tap atoms.kick4 below: popover with Derive / Detach / Go to card. Graph > Rack loads this: one kick4 card (x1), one derived card, one loud card
$: s(atoms.kick4).gain(atoms.loud)
$: s(atoms.kick4({ n: 8 })).gain(0.5)
